definition: The TTS component predicting how long each phoneme lasts, aligning text to time in non-autoregressive systems (FastSpeech lineage).
details: The TTS component predicting how long each phoneme lasts, aligning text to time in non-autoregressive systems (FastSpeech lineage). Duration errors produce rushed, smeared, or droning speech.

explainer.lead: A duration model decides how long each sound in a text-to-speech system should last. This timing helps synthetic speech sound naturally paced rather than rushed, smeared, or monotonously drawn out.

tiers.eli5: Reading aloud is like stretching each sound to fit the rhythm of a sentence. A duration model tells a speech computer how long to hold every sound, so it does not race through some parts and drone through others.
tiers.practitioner: In non-autoregressive TTS, including the FastSpeech lineage, the duration model supplies per-phoneme timing used to align text with speech. Inspect predicted durations when output sounds rushed, smeared, or droning; correcting overall speed alone may not fix uneven phoneme timing.
tiers.paperLevel: For phonemes p1...pn, a duration model predicts d1...dn, where di is the duration assigned to phoneme pi. These predictions align the phoneme sequence to time in non-autoregressive synthesis, as in the FastSpeech lineage; duration errors can produce rushed, smeared, or droning speech.

explainer.example: For four phonemes, the model might predict durations of 2, 3, 2, and 5 speech frames. The result spans 12 frames, with the final phoneme held longest.

usedIn.name: FastSpeech-lineage TTS
usedIn.detail: Predicts phoneme durations for non-autoregressive text-to-speech alignment.

usedIn.name: Non-autoregressive speech synthesis
usedIn.detail: Maps text sounds to time so generated speech has appropriate pacing.

explainer.intuition: Text says which sounds to make, but not exactly how long to hold each one. The duration model supplies that missing timing, one phoneme at a time.
howItWorks: Start with the sequence of phonemes to be spoken.
Predict a duration for each phoneme.
Use those durations to place the phonemes along a timeline.
Generate speech that follows the resulting alignment.
explainer.whyItMatters: Per-phoneme timing is central to intelligible, natural-sounding pacing. Poor duration predictions can make speech hurried, blurred together, or unnaturally sustained.
misconceptions: It does not choose which phonemes to speak; it predicts how long the given phonemes last.
It controls more than overall speaking speed: individual sounds can still be badly timed.

diagram.caption: The duration model turns a phoneme sequence into the timing used for speech generation.
